review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

7:1.sourceText: Οὗτος γὰρ ὁ Μελχισέδεκ, βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ, ἱερεὺς τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου, ὁ συναντήσας Ἀβραὰμ ὑποστρέφοντι ἀπὸ τῆς κοπῆς τῶν βασιλέων καὶ εὐλογήσας αὐτόν,
7:1.targetText: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham turning back from the striking of the kings, and blessed him,

7:2.sourceText: ᾧ καὶ δεκάτην ἀπὸ πάντων ἐμέρισεν Ἀβραάμ, πρῶτον μὲν ἑρμηνευόμενος βασιλεὺς δικαιοσύνης, ἔπειτα δὲ καὶ βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ, ὅ ἐστιν βασιλεὺς εἰρήνης,
7:2.targetText: to whom also Abraham divided a tenth of all (first, indeed, being interpreted, “King of righteousness,” and then also, “King of Salem,” which is, King of Peace),

7:3.sourceText: ἀπάτωρ, ἀμήτωρ, ἀγενεαλόγητος, μήτε ἀρχὴν ἡμερῶν μήτε ζωῆς τέλος ἔχων, ἀφωμοιωμένος δὲ τῷ Υἱῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ, μένει ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸ διηνεκές.
7:3.targetText: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, and having been like the Son of God, remains a priest continually.

groups.note: The whole adverbial εἰς τὸ διηνεκές means continuously/continually; LSV renders that real preposition-article-continuous constituent with one adverb, without inventing separate English destination or article words.

7:4.sourceText: Θεωρεῖτε δὲ πηλίκος οὗτος ᾧ δεκάτην Ἀβραὰμ ἔδωκεν ἐκ τῶν ἀκροθινίων ὁ πατριάρχης.
7:4.targetText: And see how great this one [is], to whom Abraham the patriarch also gave a tenth out of the best of the spoils,

groups.note: The actual ἀκροθίνια noun denotes top/choice spoils; English best of the spoils expands that one compound noun, not independently written Greek best and spoils heads.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.
Source-witness connective addition: LSV also follows the longer καί reading; pinned N1904 has no additive connector in the Abraham-gave clause.

7:5.sourceText: καὶ οἱ μὲν ἐκ τῶν υἱῶν Λευεὶ τὴν ἱερατείαν λαμβάνοντες ἐντολὴν ἔχουσιν ἀποδεκατοῖν τὸν λαὸν κατὰ τὸν νόμον, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτῶν, καίπερ ἐξεληλυθότας ἐκ τῆς ὀσφύος Ἀβραάμ·
7:5.targetText: and those, indeed, out of the sons of Levi receiving the priesthood, have a command to take tithes from the people according to the Law, that is, their brothers, even though they came forth out of the loins of Abraham;

groups.note: The actual tithe-collecting verb ἀποδεκατοῖν takes the people as its object; LSV to take tithes from expresses that same collecting relation with English from, not an extra Greek taking verb or preposition.
The actual perfect plural coming-forth participle is recast as the finite English they came forth, retaining its same plural people subject and descent predicate.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

7:6.sourceText: ὁ δὲ μὴ γενεαλογούμενος ἐξ αὐτῶν δεδεκάτωκεν Ἀβραάμ, καὶ τὸν ἔχοντα τὰς ἐπαγγελίας εὐλόγηκεν.
7:6.targetText: and he who was not reckoned by genealogy of them, received tithes from Abraham, and he has blessed him having the promises,

groups.note: The actual present genealogy/reckoning participle γενεαλογούμενος is rendered was reckoned by genealogy; English expands that one predicate into its genealogical reckoning sense and uses past was without changing the pinned present form.

The actual perfect tithe-collecting verb δεδεκάτωκεν is rendered received tithes from with the same Abraham payer relation; no independently written receive verb or from preposition is added to the original.

7:7.sourceText: χωρὶς δὲ πάσης ἀντιλογίας τὸ ἔλαττον ὑπὸ τοῦ κρείττονος εὐλογεῖται.
7:7.targetText: and apart from all controversy, the less is blessed by the better—

7:8.sourceText: καὶ ὧδε μὲν δεκάτας ἀποθνῄσκοντες ἄνθρωποι λαμβάνουσιν, ἐκεῖ δὲ μαρτυρούμενος ὅτι ζῇ.
7:8.targetText: and here, indeed, men who die receive tithes, and there [he] who is testified to that he was living,

groups.note: The actual masculine passive testifying participle is substantival for the person attested; English he who supplies that participial person/relative support and is belongs to the written passive predicate. It is not a separately printed Greek he pronoun.
Pinned ζῇ is the present lives; LSV he was living recasts it as past progressive while retaining that same living predicate and encoded third-person subject.

7:9.sourceText: καὶ ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, δι’ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Λευεὶς ὁ δεκάτας λαμβάνων δεδεκάτωται·
7:9.targetText: and so to speak, through Abraham even Levi who is receiving tithes, has paid tithes,

groups.note: The actual ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν is the parenthetical as-a-word-to-say idiom, rendered so to speak as a whole constituent.

The actual perfect passive tithe verb says Levi has been tithed; English has paid tithes recasts the same paying/being-tithed event from its participant role, not an independently printed Greek pay verb.

7:10.sourceText: ἔτι γὰρ ἐν τῇ ὀσφύϊ τοῦ πατρὸς ἦν ὅτε συνήντησεν αὐτῷ Μελχισέδεκ.
7:10.targetText: for he was yet in the loins of the father when Melchizedek met him.

7:11.sourceText: Εἰ μὲν οὖν τελείωσις διὰ τῆς Λευειτικῆς ἱερωσύνης ἦν, ὁ λαὸς γὰρ ἐπ’ αὐτῆς νενομοθέτηται, τίς ἔτι χρεία κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ ἕτερον ἀνίστασθαι ἱερέα καὶ οὐ κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Ἀαρὼν λέγεσθαι;
7:11.targetText: If indeed, then, perfection were through the Levitical priesthood—for the people under it had received law—what further need, according to the order of Melchizedek, for another priest to arise, and not to be called according to the order of Aaron?

groups.note: The actual perfect passive lawgiving verb νενομοθέτηται describes the people as legislated for; LSV had received law expresses the same reception of legislation without substituting a separate Greek receiving verb or law noun.
The accusative priest is the subject of the arise infinitive; English for marks that same infinitival-subject relation, not a separately written source preposition.

7:12.sourceText: μετατιθεμένης γὰρ τῆς ἱερωσύνης ἐξ ἀνάγκης καὶ νόμου μετάθεσις γίνεται.
7:12.targetText: For the priesthood being changed, of necessity also, a change comes of the Law,

groups.note: The actual becoming/occurring verb γίνεται is rendered comes in the occurrence sense, not as a different Greek arriving/travel verb.

7:13.sourceText: ἐφ’ ὃν γὰρ λέγεται ταῦτα, φυλῆς ἑτέρας μετέσχηκεν, ἀφ’ ἧς οὐδεὶς προσέσχηκεν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ·
7:13.targetText: for He of whom these things are said in another tribe has had part, of whom no one gave attendance at the altar,

groups.note: The actual preposition plus substantive relative ἐφ’ ὃν introduces the person concerning whom these things are said; English He of whom expands that real relative person relation without a separate written He pronoun.

The actual genitive tribe is the complement of sharing/partaking; English in another tribe has had part states that same tribal membership relation with in, not a separately written source in preposition.
The actual feminine singular relative ἧς refers to the tribe, from which; LSV of whom treats the tribe through its members, retaining the same antecedent with the grammatical recast explicit.

7:14.sourceText: πρόδηλον γὰρ ὅτι ἐξ Ἰούδα ἀνατέταλκεν ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν, εἰς ἣν φυλὴν περὶ ἱερέων οὐδὲν Μωϋσῆς ἐλάλησεν.
7:14.targetText: for [it is] evident that out of Judah has arisen our Lord, in regard to which tribe Moses spoke nothing concerning priesthood.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

Source-witness lexical difference: pinned N1904 has plural ἱερέων, priests/persons; LSV priesthood follows the TR office noun ἱερωσύνης. These are related priestly concepts but not the same lexical noun, so no office-noun identity is assigned to the actual persons noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness lexical difference: LSV follows TR ἱερωσύνης, the priesthood office, whereas pinned N1904 prints ἱερέων, plural priests. Contextual priestly relation does not supply an identical office-noun head.
English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

7:15.sourceText: Καὶ περισσότερον ἔτι κατάδηλόν ἐστιν, εἰ κατὰ τὴν ὁμοιότητα Μελχισέδεκ ἀνίσταται ἱερεὺς ἕτερος,
7:15.targetText: And it is yet more abundantly most evident, if according to the likeness of Melchizedek there arises another priest,

7:16.sourceText: ὃς οὐ κατὰ νόμον ἐντολῆς σαρκίνης γέγονεν ἀλλὰ κατὰ δύναμιν ζωῆς ἀκαταλύτου.
7:16.targetText: who did not come according to the law of a fleshly command, but according to the power of an endless life,

groups.note: The actual perfect become/come-to-be verb γέγονεν concerns becoming priest; LSV did come retains that status-coming-into-being predicate, not a Greek spatial coming verb.
The actual ἀκατάλυτος adjective is indestructible/indissoluble; English endless renders that enduring life quality without substituting a different Greek endless adjective.

7:17.sourceText: μαρτυρεῖται γὰρ ὅτι Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ.
7:17.targetText: for He testifies, “You [are] a priest—throughout the age, according to the order of Melchizedek”;

groups.note: Pinned μαρτυρεῖται is passive is attested/it is testified, whereas TR μαρτυρεῖ and LSV use active testifies. The actual testimony predicate is retained with its voice/subject recast explicit; the English personal agent He is separately explained, not assigned to an implicit passive patient.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual ὅτι introduces the attested quotation; English uses direct quotation without a separate that.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English active personal agent follows the active-witness rendering; pinned N1904 passive μαρτυρεῖται does not print that personal agent. The same testifying head is retained, but a source subject/agent pronoun is not invented.
English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

7:18.sourceText: ἀθέτησις μὲν γὰρ γίνεται προαγούσης ἐντολῆς διὰ τὸ αὐτῆς ἀσθενὲς καὶ ἀνωφελές,
7:18.targetText: for an annulling indeed comes of the command going before because of its weakness, and unprofitableness

groups.note: The actual article with the weak adjective nominalizes the weakness quality; LSV uses the abstraction noun weakness, not a separate source noun.
The actual unprofitable adjective is coordinated under the same substantive quality construction; English unprofitableness names that quality without a separately written abstraction noun.

7:19.sourceText: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐτελείωσεν ὁ νόμος, ἐπεισαγωγὴ δὲ κρείττονος ἐλπίδος, δι’ ἧς ἐγγίζομεν τῷ Θεῷ.
7:19.targetText: (for nothing did the Law perfect), and the bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.

7:20.sourceText: Καὶ καθ’ ὅσον οὐ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας, —οἱ μὲν γὰρ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας εἰσὶν ἱερεῖς γεγονότες,
7:20.targetText: And inasmuch as [it is] not apart from oath

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

sourceMoved.reason: The complete first contrast clause, those indeed for apart from oath have become priests, is printed in LSV7:21 rather than7:20.

7:21.sourceText: ὁ δὲ μετὰ ὁρκωμοσίας διὰ τοῦ λέγοντος πρὸς αὐτόν Ὤμοσεν Κύριος, καὶ οὐ μεταμεληθήσεται Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα·
7:21.targetText: (for those indeed apart from oath have become priests, and He [became priest] with an oath through Him who is saying to Him, “The LORD swore, and will not regret, You [are] a priest throughout the age, according to the order of Melchizedek”),

groups.note: The actual εἰσιν ... γεγονότες periphrastic have-become predicate is stated with the first priests and inherited in the immediately contrasted He clause. LSV repeats its becoming predicate as bracketed became, changing the supplied repetition to singular for the same contrast. The same written source identities support both genuine realizations; no second Greek becoming predicate is invented.

The actual plural priests predicate is shared by the immediate those/He contrast. LSV repeats its priest designation in the singular bracketed became priest ellipse for He, preserving that real predicate relation without a second written Greek priest noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

unmappedTarget.text: according to the order of Melchizedek
unmappedTarget.reason: The longer witness repeats the order-of-Melchizedek clause here; pinned N1904 ends the quotation at age. Its genuine words in7:17 are not borrowed to manufacture a second source quotation here.

7:22.sourceText: —κατὰ τοσοῦτο καὶ κρείττονος διαθήκης γέγονεν ἔγγυος Ἰησοῦς.
7:22.targetText: by so much also has Jesus become guarantee of a better covenant,

7:23.sourceText: Καὶ οἱ μὲν πλείονές εἰσιν γεγονότες ἱερεῖς διὰ τὸ θανάτῳ κωλύεσθαι παραμένειν·
7:23.targetText: and those indeed are many who have become priests, because by death they are hindered from remaining;

groups.note: The actual διά plus articular infinitive introduces the causal hindrance clause; English because renders that full causal construction without a separate English article.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV recasts the periphrastic have-become-priests predicate and many as those are many who have become priests, inserting an English relative frame. The Greek has no separately printed relative pronoun; its actual being and becoming heads retain their own English verbs.

review.note: The written εἰσιν γεγονότες periphrastic perfect is recast as two English predicates, are many and have become priests. Both real verbal forms remain linked; the English relative who is separately supplied.

7:24.sourceText: ὁ δὲ διὰ τὸ μένειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἀπαράβατον ἔχει τὴν ἱερωσύνην·
7:24.targetText: and He, because of His remaining throughout the age, has the inviolable priesthood,

groups.note: The actual accusative αὐτόν is the subject of the remaining infinitive; English His turns that same subject into a possessive with the gerund, not a written Greek genitive possessive.
The actual ἀπαράβατος adjective denotes untransferable/permanent priesthood; LSV inviolable keeps this adjective head without replacing it by a different Greek quality.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article nominalizes the remaining infinitive; LSV uses His remaining with no separate article.

7:25.sourceText: ὅθεν καὶ σῴζειν εἰς τὸ παντελὲς δύναται τοὺς προσερχομένους δι’ αὐτοῦ τῷ Θεῷ, πάντοτε ζῶν εἰς τὸ ἐντυγχάνειν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν.
7:25.targetText: from where also He is able to save to the very end, those coming through Him to God—ever living to make intercession for them.

groups.note: The actual εἰς τὸ παντελές is the full uttermost/completely adverbial constituent. LSV to the very end expresses its enduring/completeness interpretation; no separate Greek end noun or temporal proposition is invented.
The actual εἰς τὸ articular-infinitive construction marks the purpose of living, English to make intercession; the preposition and article jointly supply this purpose connector.

7:26.sourceText: Τοιοῦτος γὰρ ἡμῖν καὶ ἔπρεπεν ἀρχιερεύς, ὅσιος, ἄκακος, ἀμίαντος, κεχωρισμένος ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν, καὶ ὑψηλότερος τῶν οὐρανῶν γενόμενος·
7:26.targetText: For also such a Chief Priest was fitting for us—holy, innocent, undefiled, separate from the sinners, and having become higher than the heavens,

7:27.sourceText: ὃς οὐκ ἔχει καθ’ ἡμέραν ἀνάγκην, ὥσπερ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς, πρότερον ὑπὲρ τῶν ἰδίων ἁμαρτιῶν θυσίας ἀναφέρειν, ἔπειτα τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ· τοῦτο γὰρ ἐποίησεν ἐφάπαξ ἑαυτὸν ἀνενέγκας.
7:27.targetText: who has no daily necessity, as the chief priests, to first offer up sacrifice for His own sins, then for those of the people; for this He did once, having offered up Himself;

groups.note: The one actual ὑπέρ governs the coordinated own-sins then people’s-sins objects. English repeats for in the second coordinated ellipse; both genuine realizations retain this same source preposition rather than a second invented one.
The actual plural sacrifices noun is rendered singular collective sacrifice; the same sacrificial head is retained with the number difference explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

7:28.sourceText: ὁ νόμος γὰρ ἀνθρώπους καθίστησιν ἀρχιερεῖς ἔχοντας ἀσθένειαν, ὁ λόγος δὲ τῆς ὁρκωμοσίας τῆς μετὰ τὸν νόμον Υἱόν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τετελειωμένον.
7:28.targetText: for the Law appoints men [as] chief priests, having weakness, but the word of the oath that [is] after the Law [appoints] the Son having been perfected throughout the age.

groups.note: The actual appointing predicate is stated for the Law and inherited in the immediately contrasted word-of-the-oath clause. LSV explicitly repeats it as bracketed appoints; both uses retain the one real original predicate rather than an invented second verb.
The actual chief-priests accusative is the predicate complement of appoints; English as makes that grammatical role explicit, without a separately printed Greek as preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: English inserts is in the relative after-the-Law modifier. The Greek article plus temporal prepositional phrase is verbless; the separate actual appointing predicate is not a copula for this modifier.
